explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1093. The pairs (k, n) with n ≥ 2k range over binomial coefficients C(n,k) whose deficiency is defined, meaning every prime factor of C(n,k) exceeds k. Deficiency is the number of 0 ≤ i < k with n - i k-smooth, implemented as smoothNumbers (k+1). The question asks whether infinitely many have deficiency 1. The degenerate k = 0, 1 cases have deficiency 0 and do not interfere. As a sanity check, C(7,3) = 35 has deficiency 1 (only 6 is 3-smooth), matching the page.
